name: Franklin
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Franklin, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Franklin, MA: Santa on the Town Common, the FPAC Nutcracker, A Wreath of Franklin, the Dean College lighting and library holiday fun.
lede: Franklin rings in Christmas with Santa arriving on the Town Common by fire truck, a homegrown Nutcracker with more than 100 area dancers, and a downtown wreath celebration run by the town's arts and culture office.
celebrates: The town's Arts, Culture and Creative Economy office gathers the season under Frosty Franklin Festivities, a list of downtown arts, family programs and local shopping. Christmas on the Common is planned each year by a group of Franklin residents and paid for entirely by donations: Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive by fire truck, DJ Mike and Jingles the Elf entertain, and children get cookies, cocoa and a gift. FPAC Holiday Productions stages The Nutcracker and its own musical, 'Tis the Season. Dean College lights its holiday display on Awpie Way, and A Wreath of Franklin fills downtown with decorated wreaths.
lastyear: In 2025 the Franklin Cultural District listed a full run of holiday events. The Franklin Public Library held a Santa Storywalk on November 29, and Santa arrived on the Town Common on Sunday, November 30, at 4 pm, riding a Franklin fire truck in an event sponsored by Concerts on the Common. FPAC staged The Nutcracker on December 6 and 7, the Senior Center held a Winter Wonderland for the whole community on December 11, A Wreath of Franklin filled downtown on December 13, and FPAC closed the season with Humbug on December 20 and 21.
facts: Franklin was incorporated in 1778. The town had planned to call itself Exeter but chose Franklin to honor Dr. Benjamin Franklin, and the town's library is considered America's first public library. A Wreath of Franklin reaches its third year in 2026 with the theme The Magic We Make and more than 50 pop-up arts vendors. FPAC first presented its holiday musical 'Tis the Season in 1995, and its Nutcracker has been a Franklin tradition for more than 25 years.
trains: Franklin sits at the end of the MBTA Franklin/Foxboro Line, with commuter rail stops at the Franklin/Dean College station downtown and at Forge Park/495, so a ride into Boston can be part of a holiday day out. The town's own wreath program points visitors to the Franklin/Dean MBTA lot for parking downtown. For a train ride with Christmas lights, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train, and the Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River is within a drive.

traditions: Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive on the Franklin Town Common by fire truck, with music, cocoa and a gift for each child, all paid for by donations.
FPAC Holiday Productions has staged The Nutcracker with a live orchestra and more than 100 area dancers for more than 25 years.
FPAC's original holiday musical, first presented in 1995, returns each December with holiday classics in styles from Motown to Broadway.
The town's arts office fills downtown with community wreaths and a pop-up arts market, and the day kicks off Franklin Restaurant Week.
Dean College invites the Franklin community to its annual holiday lighting on Awpie Way, with student performances and hot chocolate.
The Franklin Public Library turns a winter story into an indoor walk of crafts and activities that ends with a visit to Santa.
kidfact: Franklin is named after Benjamin Franklin, the man who flew a kite in a storm. He sent the town a gift of books, and that gift started what is called the first public library in America.
faq: When does Santa come to the Franklin Town Common?

Santa visits the Town Common at Christmas on the Common, usually on the Sunday after Thanksgiving in the late afternoon. In 2025 he arrived on November 30 at 4 pm on a Franklin fire truck. The event is planned by Franklin residents and paid for by donations, with cookies, cocoa and a gift from Santa for the children.
Where can kids see The Nutcracker in Franklin?

The Franklin Performing Arts Company stages The Nutcracker each December at the Franklin High School Auditorium on Oak Street. The production has a live orchestra, special guest artists and more than 100 area dancers, and FPAC calls it a holiday tradition of more than 25 years. Tickets are sold through FPAC's website.
What is A Wreath of Franklin?

A Wreath of Franklin is a December day of holiday shopping, arts and community programs in downtown Franklin, run by the town's Arts, Culture and Creative Economy office. Residents build weatherproof wreaths that are displayed downtown, more than 50 artists sell at pop-up markets, and the day opens Franklin Restaurant Week.
Does Dean College have a tree lighting?

Yes. Every year Dean College welcomes the Franklin community to its holiday lighting on Awpie Way. The college describes holiday entertainment and performances by Dean students, hot chocolate to stay warm and plenty of holiday spirit. Dean lists the lighting among its annual traditions.
Can we take the train to Franklin?

Yes. The MBTA Franklin/Foxboro Line commuter rail stops at Franklin/Dean College in downtown Franklin and at Forge Park/495. The town's wreath program lists the Franklin/Dean MBTA lot among the downtown parking options for its December events, along with lots at THE BLACK BOX on West Central Street and the Franklin Public Library on Main Street.
